PRESCHOOL · AGE 3 · CLASS 3 MAGIC ACTIVITY

Look & Draw — Magic Shapes

Look at a picture, then draw your own — right on the page. Twenty-five pictures are waiting on four shelves: magic shapes, garden friends, opposites and fruits. Six big colors, an eraser, undo, and a Save button for your very own artwork. Grown-ups stay close; little artists lead.

No scores, no timers — just you and your drawing. Your drawings stay on this page until you close it, and Save keeps one forever.

CHOOSE A PICTURE

What shall we draw first?

Pick a picture from any shelf, look closely at it, then draw your own on the big white canvas. Your drawing waits for you if you switch pictures — and you can start over any time.

Magic shapes

Garden friends

Drawings you have already made stay saved while this page is open — switching pictures never erases them.

LOOK & DRAW · THE HOUSE

Draw the house.

Look at the picture: A square wall, a triangle roof and a rectangle door. Now draw your own on the big white canvas. Every drawing is right — this is your artwork.

Pick a color, then draw with your finger, mouse or stylus.

For grown-ups: ask your artist — “Can you find the shapes in your drawing?”

OFF-SCREEN PLAY

Pictures you can draw anywhere.

The best drawing table costs nothing. Pick one of these and let your child lead — the looking and the drawing do the teaching all by themselves.

Big paper, big shapes

  • Tape a big sheet of paper to the table and draw the house together with crayons — triangle roof, square wall, rectangle door. Say each shape name out loud as you draw it.

Chalk shapes outside

  • Draw giant shapes on the pavement with chalk, then walk, hop or jump along the outline of each one. Big movements make shape words stick.

Draw what you see

  • Hunt the house for circles, squares, triangles and rectangles — a plate, a book, a slice of toast — and draw the best ones in your own shape museum.

One safety word for this game: chunky crayons and washable chalk only, and grown-ups handle any sticky tape. Keep pencils away from little mouths — artists this age still explore with them.

ACTIVITY COMPLETE

Pictures everywhere you look!

Circles, squares, triangles, ovals — petals, wings, wheels and windows — are now things your child draws on purpose: on the canvas, on paper and in the pavement. Whether you drew one picture or twenty-five, that was real looking and real drawing, and every drawing was already right.

FOR GROWN-UPS

How drawing teaches looking.

This activity deliberately has no wrong answers. The reference picture stays beside the canvas so your child can look back and forth — noticing that a roof is a triangle or a grape is a circle is the whole lesson, and it happens inside ordinary drawing. The gallery gathers the pictures from the Age 3 games your child may already have played, so the flower, the ball, the door and the eight fruits all live here now. "Show me how" reads a few short steps aloud and shows them as plain text you can follow together; nothing is ever drawn for your child and nothing is graded.

The tools are honest: six colors, three brush sizes, a real eraser, undo for oops-moments, clear for fresh starts, and Save — which downloads your child’s own canvas only, never the reference picture. Drawings for each picture stay while the page stays open, so switching to the rocket and back will not erase the house. Nothing is uploaded anywhere, and closing the tab lets the gallery go — that is what Save is for.

Works with finger, mouse or stylus on phones, tablets and desktops. The Calm Mode toggle in the footer (or your device’s reduced-motion setting) stills every animation while drawing, tools and steps keep working.

FAMILY FEEDBACK

How was this activity?

Your feedback helps us make Kiddo School better. This is feedback about the activity, for the grown-ups who make it — it is never about a child.

Comments stay short and are read by the school office before they appear. Don’t include private information — no surnames, ages or addresses.
